assessment.summary: A continent-scale disaster with extremely low annual probability and no current signs of imminent eruption.
assessment.timeframe: No reliable short-term forecast. The three largest past eruptions occurred ~2.1M, ~1.3M, and ~0.64M years ago.

claims.text: The USGS estimates the yearly probability of another Yellowstone caldera-forming eruption at roughly 1 in 730,000 (0.00014%), based on averaging the intervals between the three past major eruptions.

USGS states Yellowstone's three caldera-forming eruptions were the Huckleberry Ridge Tuff (~2.1 million years ago), the Mesa Falls Tuff (~1.3 million years ago), and the Lava Creek Tuff (~640,000 years ago).

description: A large caldera system beneath Yellowstone National Park capable of a 'supereruption' that would blanket much of North America in ash and inject climate-altering aerosols into the stratosphere. Such eruptions are extraordinarily rare and there is no evidence one is imminent.
name: Yellowstone Supervolcano
